summary: Both P1 outcomes land and I verified the load-bearing mechanisms independently: the standalone `tasks_from: internal_tls` entry works with the hoisted gate, and throttle-on-a-handler serializes strictly while still letting a failed host's peers run and still exiting non-zero. Converge behaviour and the drift signal are unchanged. Three advisory findings, none blocking: check-mode no longer surfaces the kubelite restart, /livez is a weaker signal than the comment's 'serving again', and Restart openbao is left outside the limit its sibling reload now carries.

findings.summary: The kubelite restart handler is a shell task, so a --check --diff run skips it and (with display_skipped_hosts=False) never names the control-plane bounce an apply will do.
The wait gates on /livez (and kubelet healthz on a worker), which omit etcd-readiness/informer-sync — weaker than the 'only once this one is serving' the handler comment claims.
Reload openbao gained throttle: 1 but the more disruptive Restart openbao in the same role still relies on the caller's serial.
